comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C2, C29-C33 regarding sample size, exclusion criteria, and ethical approval. Both evaluations find these methodological details adequately documented and supported.
Perfect agreement on claims C15-C17 regarding risk preference consistency, variance, and polarization. Both evaluations accept these findings about individual differences in social influence effects.

Perfect agreement on claims C18-C21 regarding vmPFC tracking of decision probability. Both evaluations accept the fMRI evidence with appropriate corrections and find it consistent with prior literature.
Perfect agreement on claims C24, C66 regarding TPJ engagement during social observation. Both evaluations endorse this as a key neural finding supporting the social simulation mechanism.

Both support claim C25 regarding dmPFC sensitivity to social context. OpenEval notes caution due to uncorrected p-value, while peer reviewers suggest broader interpretation beyond conflict monitoring to include information updating.
Perfect agreement on claims C72-C74 regarding mPFC axis organization distinguishing self and other valuations. Both evaluations accept this finding as consistent with prior literature.
Perfect agreement on claims C77-C82 regarding self-report validation of model parameters. Both evaluations accept these findings as supporting evidence for the social influence mechanism.

Strong agreement on claims C37-C63 regarding theoretical framing and interpretation. Both evaluations endorse the citations and interpretations. Peer reviewers additionally request contextualization to young adults regarding lifespan differences.

Both address claims C26-C28, C58, C67 regarding connectivity findings. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to insufficient sample size (C83), while peer reviewers accept the findings but note authors' own caution about sample size.

Both address claims C7, C11 regarding main effects and control conditions. OpenEval focuses on ruling out practice effects, while peer reviewers emphasize the convincing evidence of choice adjustment based on observer type.

Both address learning phase results (C4-C6). OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation, while peer reviewers implicitly accept that participants successfully learned partner preferences without questioning the results.

Both address model comparison (C12, C65). OpenEval emphasizes model validation through iBIC and parameter recovery, while peer reviewers praise the model selection approach for understanding cognitive processes.
Partial overlap on task design claims C34, C35, C68. OpenEval focuses on learning manipulation success, while peer reviewers praise the overall task design as well-designed and novel.
Partial overlap on methodological details C70, C71. OpenEval notes standard procedures adequately documented, while peer reviewers praise the comprehensive task design including these elements.
Partial overlap on claims C13, C14. OpenEval emphasizes model validation through behavioral correlations, while peer reviewers accept the overall pattern of choice adjustment.

Partial overlap on lateralized connectivity findings C75, C76. OpenEval rates overall connectivity as UNCERTAIN due to sample size, while peer reviewers accept lateralized findings as complementary to bilateral results.
Both address claim C3 regarding initial belief findings. OpenEval provides specific statistical evidence (p=0.0495), while peer reviewers implicitly accept the finding without detailed discussion.

Both address claim C83 regarding sample size limitation for mediation. OpenEval rates overall connectivity as UNCERTAIN citing this limitation, while peer reviewers accept the authors' acknowledgment of this constraint.

Minimal overlap on claim C64 regarding central hypothesis. OpenEval links statistical evidence to hypothesis support, while peer reviewers endorse the broader theoretical framing and differentiated adjustment interpretation.

Minimal overlap on claim C69 regarding parameter recovery. OpenEval emphasizes this as part of model validation, while peer reviewers praise the overall task design without specifically discussing parameter recovery.
